name: Kneeling Leg Curl
description: The kneeling leg curl is performed with the feet anchored and the knees on a padded surface, using the hamstrings to curl the body toward the heels from a kneeling position with the torso upright. Unlike the Nordic hamstring curl which is a full eccentric movement, the kneeling leg curl is a concentric-focused variation that develops hamstring strength closer to the shortened position and serves as a bridge exercise between machine curls and the Nordic curl.

execution.starting_position: Kneel on a padded surface with the feet anchored behind (use a partner, barbell, or machine). Start with the torso vertical over the knees.
execution.setup_instructions: Have a partner hold the ankles or wedge the heels under a barbell secured at floor height. Knee padding is essential.
steps: Step 1: Kneel upright with feet anchored and hips extended.
Step 2: Lower the torso forward a small amount, then use the hamstrings to pull the body back upright — the motion is a 'pull toward the heels' action.
Step 3: Hold the upright position briefly, then lower forward under control.
Step 4: Repeat for the prescribed reps, controlling both phases.
Step 5: Avoid falling too far forward — this transitions into a Nordic curl and should be progressed to separately.
execution.breathing_instructions: Exhale as you pull up. Inhale as you lower.
common_mistakes: Hinging at the hip (the motion should come from knee flexion, not hip hinging)
Swinging the torso rather than contracting the hamstrings
Moving through a range the hamstrings cannot control
safety_considerations: If unable to perform even a minimal controlled range, begin with machine leg curls to build hamstring strength first
Knee padding is essential to prevent bruising
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Work in the range the hamstrings can actively control — typically 20–60° initially.
coaching_cues: Pull your heels toward your glutes — think of it like a standing leg curl
Keep the hips extended — don't fold forward at the hip
Own both directions — control the lowering too
